title: pr-review-scratchpad-kv-cache-batching-ethan-roberts
content:
Context:

Quick scratchpad for PR #1427 (kv-cache + batching refactor). Mostly notes for follow-ups and things to ask in the next sync. This is messy — notes to self and a checklist that I’ll convert to a PR comment later.

Summary:
- PR attempts to unify prefix/KV cache handling across multiple model backends and introduce a continuous batching path for short-context requests.
- Major goals: reduce per-token latency for common short requests, avoid duplicate KV lookups, and make cache invalidation explicit for versioned models.

Quick high-level checklist (what I looked for):
- [ ] Correctness: no regressions for chat history replay & multi-turn streaming
- [ ] Race conditions: concurrent requests hitting same cache key while eviction/refresh happening
- [ ] Performance: end-to-end latency numbers + p50/p95 before/after for small (<=32) seqs
- [ ] Metrics: instrumentation for cache hits/misses, evictions, and batching efficiency
- [ ] Tests: unit + integration (simulated concurrency) + perf smoke tests

Notes / findings:
- Implementation moves KVCache into a shared module (kv_cache/shared_cache.go) and exposes a lightweight interface. Nice — reduces duplicated logic across backends.
- Concern: the cache key currently includes model_version but not model_variant (quantized vs fp16). Need to confirm PR includes variant in key. Otherwise we risk serving wrong kv blobs to incompatible executors.
- Batching path: adds a ContinuousBatcher with a max_batch_ms of 8 and max_batch_size of 64. Default looks reasonable, but we should make these configurable per-model via model config.
- Observability: emits two new metrics: kv_cache_lookup_ms and batch_wait_ms. Good. Missing: per-key eviction_count and a tag for model_variant.

Potential correctness issues to call out in review:
1) Cache invalidation edge case: when model is rolled back to previous version the code relies on TTL to expire keys. For dedicated/private customers with long-lived instances TTL might be long — consider explicit versioned namespace prefix to avoid stale keys.
2) Concurrency: in shared_cache.Put we do a get-then-put without a lock; there is an in-memory map and a concurrent goroutine that evicts. Looks racy — need to ensure atomic CompareAndSwap behavior or use sync.Map. Add a test that runs N goroutines doing Put/Get/Delete repeatedly.
3) Streaming + KV: when streaming, we append tokens progressively and sometimes write partial KV material. Ensure that partial writes are not visible to other requests (use write-ahead staging key).

Refactor ideas / follow-ups:
- Move key-generation into a single helper with unit tests for all model/version/variant combinations. (small PR)
- Add a flush-on-rollout hook in the deployment manager so that model version rollouts can trigger eviction of keys for the previous model id. (medium)
- Expose per-model batching configs in model catalog (ui + API). In particular, allow smaller max_batch_ms for latency-sensitive customers.
- Consider a two-tier cache: in-process small LRU for ultra-low latency and remote shared cache (redis/memcache) for cross-worker reuse. Document tradeoffs.

Testing TODOs (prioritize before merging):
- [ ] unit: key-gen tests across variants + versions
- [ ] integration: run runtime with simulated requests hitting same conversation id concurrently (use existing test harness)
- [ ] perf: p50/p95 numbers for seq len 8/16/32 with and without batching enabled
- [ ] chaos: eviction under memory pressure (simulate high mem usage)

Questions to ask PR author (Maya):
- Did you intentionally omit model_variant in the cache key? If so, why?
- Is there an intended migration plan for existing cached blobs when we change key format?
- Are batching params tunable per-model (I couldn’t find the mapping in model_catalog table)?

Suggested inline comments for PR:
- line 78: add comment explaining why we don't use sync.Map here — if no good reason, switch to sync.Map or add mutex
- line 143: key generation lacks variant: include variant and add unit test
- line 210: batching queue uses time.After for flush; use a time.Timer.Reset pattern to avoid goroutine growth
- line 278: metrics tag for model_variant missing — add it to kv_cache_lookup_ms

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: regression for existing long-conv workloads (memory blow-up) — mitigation: limit total cache size per-worker and surface global eviction metric; add emergency config to disable continuous batching
- Risk: serving wrong model variant’s cache blob — mitigation: require variant in key + integration test against quantized runner

Short-term action items (me):
- [ ] Leave inline PR comments for the three high-priority correctness issues (concurrency, variant in key, TTL/migration)
- [ ] Add a quick test harness script to reproduce concurrent Put/Get behavior (push to /tmp/test-harness on this branch)
- [ ] Ask infra to add eviction_count metric (tagged by model_variant) — ping Samira

Longer-term (post-merge):
- Add rollout hook and model-catalog changes, coordinate with release-engineering for migration window
- Explore two-tier cache prototype in a spike PR

Scratch area (code snippets / ideas):
- Proposed key function:
  func cacheKey(modelID, modelVer, modelVariant, conversationID string, prefixHash string) string {
    return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s:%s:%s:%s", modelID, modelVer, modelVariant, conversationID, prefixHash)
  }

- Batcher optimization: use a single goroutine per-batcher with a bounded channel and a time.Timer to flush. Avoid spawning per-request goroutines.

Links / references:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/1427
- JIRA: JIRA-INF-4523 (kv cache refactor / batching)
- Design note: confluence:infra/kv-cache-design

Next meeting: bring these points to 2026-03-03 infra sync (pinged Maya + Samira).

-- Ethan
